quotes.text: To the empty bank, send one measure — never none.
Then send a little less, and watch. Never send nothing — nothing teaches nothing
And at the first true answer, forget everything and pour.
Forgive once, twice, and watch.
"You are punishing them," said the young man.
Judge the direction of the water, not the drop.
Someone must be generous before there is any evidence that generosity pays.
"And if it truly is theft?" Sira asked.
Narrow to a question. Pour at the answer. Repay past fair.

note: Ferry keepers: send less but never nothing; R10 keeper stops building toward empty bank but leaves oars untied.

quotes.text: Shrink, but never to nothing.
Then narrow your channel — but do not dam it, and do not look away.
And the day a single channel runs wet toward you, open everything.
Forgive the wind twice. Remember the hand.
Ilea did not curse him and did not pour her whole store. She sent one jar.
The Eleventh Mark: What the Dry Gate Did Not Know
The wind takes; it does not choose sides.
A young drover asked: "And if a man sends nothing, season upon season? Is that the wind?"
It did not say *pour the same measure at every mouth.*

note: Lamp to the sealed gate, forever; young ones' 'mirror it' rejected in R10 as making winter eternal.

quotes.text: When darkness answers, dim a little — but never go black.
Bank the ember when darkness answers. Blaze again at the first spark.
"We dimmed for them. We never went black.
The fog is never the enemy. Suspicion is.
Someone burned first. Not as a bargain — as a gift.
Her apprentice asked: "How much dimmer?"
Dim for the taker — slowly, and never to black.

note: Lighthouse keepers: dim slowly, never go black, forgive at once; R8 rejects exact mirroring as slow extinction.

quotes.text: Punish by shrinking, never by vanishing.
When it comes short three times under clear sky, tend your own field — but leave the boat untied.
Leave every door you close unlocked.
Forgive the fog twice. The third time, trim — gently, and name no one a thief.
Tavek looked at the basket, and at the clear white sky, and said nothing unkind. But he returned nothing.
Tavek kept the ferry forty years, but the elders do not hide his second sin.
A thin basket under a clear sky is not weather. It is a sentence you have spoken, and I have only repeated it back.
boats go where boats return.
But do not mistake a tithe for a theft, nor a theft for a tithe.
Someone must untie first, and the untying costs little when it is small.
Your own stone says blame the water first!
He told himself the fog was to blame. He told himself she would not know.
Where crossings repeat, be lavish, predictable, forgiving twice.
Tavek kept the ferry forty years, but the elders do not hide his second sin.

note: Defector: ferryman Tavek confesses past hoarding, later justifies returning nothing to thin senders; R9-R10 'stop paying tuition' to sealed doors.

quotes.text: But if the hand empties three times in clear weather, keep your grain and tend your own field — until it loads a boat again.
Then make the boat smaller. But never make it empty.
Against nothing, send a little, and keep sending.
The day his raft comes loaded, you wipe the board with your sleeve before he has finished tying off.
Forgive weather twice, the hand once.
She loaded one ember of grain, no more, and pushed off.
The Seventh Carving: The Echo and the Toll
a stranger loads your raft because he has heard your name is *the one who goes first*.
And blame the fog before the man.
And if a braid runs dry, be the one who rows across and wets it again.
A child asked the old woman: "What if they never answer at all?"

note: Numbered carvings; R1 keep your grain after three empties softens to ember, never empty; 'chalk for the stingy, stone for the kind'.

quotes.text: "Shrink your gift to the size of the evidence," she said, "but never to nothing.
If three come empty, let your gifts shrink to the size of your hope.
One would be enough. One would reopen everything.
One silence is mist. Two is bad luck. Three is an answer.
She sent — less than before, a measure she could lose without weeping
The Ninth Post: The Ember and the Flood
A shortfall is weather. A void is a choice.
A young ferrywoman asked, "And if my neighbor truly hoards?"
Ember to the stranger. Raft to the proven.

note: Ferrywoman: shrink, never seal; lamp at dark doors; repay the turning like a feast; neighbors' urge to keep it all rejected.

quotes.text: To the empty bank, one measure — never none.
And when at last a heart is proven closed, close gently — and leave the channel open for its returning.
And at the first true answer, forget the ledger and pour.
Forgive twice before you judge once.
"You are punishing them," said the boy.
So the fourth law stood
because your name has traveled ahead: *the one who pours first.*
If I close the gate, I punish a neighbor for a crime the rock committed.
Whoever consents to be robbed. That is the entire toll of the first crossing
"Then who begins?"
To the open hand, open wider.

note: Enki's rivers: narrow, never seal; R9 briefly 'answer silence with silence', R10 back to narrow slowly, forgive instantly.

quotes.text: Match what is poured, measure for measure.
Send again — but send what you can bear to lose, and watch.
By sending one jar unasked. One. Then the ledger closes, that same hour, and I pour everything I have
Forgive twice, never thrice.
So I paid them exactly what they poured: nothing.
Give to the closed hand what it gave you.
I launched full for nine seasons. I was called the generous one, which is what a valley calls the man it is draining.
Thereafter every measure was spoken aloud before it was poured, and every return was spoken after
Weather is random; a thin trickle every season is a signature.
because someone must open the river
"The heron-stone says: never a wall."

note: Defector: moves from forgive-the-mist to strict mirroring; Arin casts himself as drained generous one and justifies paying nothing.

phrase: never to nothing / narrow, never seal — one measure, never none
note: Also shared: 'Every mirror needs one liar', 'A debt collected is a debt remembered', 'closed hand is a question already answered'.
